According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple was reportedly considering adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make setting up a new iPhone almost seamless: transferring a user's data to the new device ahead of time. In the end, however, the feature never came to fruition.

The concept was simple: if a user upgrades on a regular monthly instalment plan, why not make switching to a new phone as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported:

There are some obvious holes here. For one, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since the data transfer could only happen at the moment of shipment—a few days after ordering, unless you chose to pick the phone up in person at a store.

There are also some obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you've been using iCloud backups all along, it shouldn't come as a surprise that Apple has your data. But the average user might worry about how that data gets from one phone to another, and whether anyone handles it along the way.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system across its retail stores called "Presto" that lets staff update software while the iPhone is still in the box. It's easy to imagine this system being extended in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one ever touching your data.

Still, the feature ultimately never made it to market—and that might actually be a good thing.
